ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an organic fragment: a benzene ring is connected to a chiral/central carbon bearing OH, this carbon is then connected to a CH2, and the CH2 is connected to HN; HN is connected to an acyl carbonyl carbon, the carbonyl carbon is also connected to the R group below, and forms C=O with oxygen. On the right side is an independent pyrophosphate-like fragment, containing a P-O-P backbone; each phosphorus atom has one P=O and one additional P=O/oxygen coordination representation. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified method, first treat the R group as the wildcard *, start from the carbonyl carbon connected to R and write it as *C(=O), the carbonyl carbon is connected to the amide nitrogen to obtain *C(=O)N; after nitrogen is connected to CH2-CH(OH)-phenyl, written as NCC(O)c1ccccc1, so the organic fragment is *C(=O)NCC(O)c1ccccc1. The independent P-O-P phosphate fragment on the right is written according to static connectivity as O=P(=O)OP(=O)=O. The two fragments are not connected by a solid bond, therefore they are separated by a dot.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First visually transcribe the static connectivity in the image, ignoring every curved arrow. Convert the organic acyl-amino alcohol fragment by starting at the generic R group as wildcard *, then the carbonyl carbon C(=O), then amide nitrogen N, then CH2-CH(OH)-phenyl to give *C(=O)NCC(O)c1ccccc1. Separately convert the depicted P-O-P phosphate fragment to O=P(=O)OP(=O)=O. Join the two disconnected components with a dot, yielding *C(=O)NCC(O)c1ccccc1.O=P(=O)OP(=O)=O.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧是一个有机片段：苯环连接到一个带 OH 的手性/中心碳，该碳再连接到一个 CH2，CH2 连接到 HN；HN 连接到一个酰基羰基碳，羰基碳还连接到下方的 R 基，并与氧形成 C=O。右侧是一个独立的焦磷酸样片段，含有 P-O-P 骨架；每个磷原子各有一个 P=O 和一个额外的 P=O/氧配位表示。图中有多条弯箭头，但题目要求忽略这些箭头。推理：按指定方法先把 R 基作为通配符 *，从 R 所连的羰基碳开始写为 *C(=O)，羰基碳连接酰胺氮得到 *C(=O)N；氮后接 CH2-CH(OH)-苯基，写作 NCC(O)c1ccccc1，所以有机片段为 *C(=O)NCC(O)c1ccccc1。右侧独立的 P-O-P 磷酸片段按静态连接写为 O=P(=O)OP(=O)=O。两个片段未由实线键连接，因此用点号分隔。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription: it uses only the depicted atom connectivity after deliberately discarding curved arrows and treating the R substituent as a wildcard attachment.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as two disconnected components. From the left component identify a benzene ring attached to CH(OH)-CH2-NH-C(=O)-R, where R is represented generically and the carbonyl oxygen is double-bonded to the acyl carbon. From the right component identify a pyrophosphate-like fragment with two phosphorus atoms linked by an oxygen and each P bearing terminal oxo/oxo-like oxygens. Ignore all curved arrows and transition-state motion marks.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction to output a SMILES expression and specifically to ignore the arrows, so only atom labels and bonds in the drawing determine the answer.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply SMILES conventions: aromatic benzene as c1ccccc1; generic R/unknown substituent as wildcard *; amide fragment as *C(=O)N; the amino alcohol chain as NCC(O)c1ccccc1; disconnected molecular fragments separated by a dot; phosphorus oxo connectivity encoded as O=P(=O)OP(=O)=O.
